chunks: As for the one who contradicts regarding the death of Amir al-Mu'minin and states that he is alive and remaining, he is obdurate.

For the knowledge of his death and martyrdom is more evident and more famous than the killing of anyone else and the death of every person, and doubt in that leads to doubt in the death of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and all of his companions.

Then what became apparent from his will and the Prophet's (peace be upon him and his family) news to him: 'You will be killed and your beard will be dyed with your blood,' also invalidates this, and that is more famous than to require narrations to be reported about it.

key_terms.النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِ: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)

ai.seo_question: What is the evidence for Imam Ali's death being more famous than others in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Al-Tusi grounds this argument in the concept of *tawatur* (mass transmission), asserting that Imam Ali’s death is a self-evident historical fact known to all Muslims, thereby making denial a form of stubbornness (*mukabbir*) rather than legitimate doubt. He links this certainty to the Prophet’s specific prophecy of Ali’s blood-dyed beard, using it to reinforce the continuity of prophetic authority and the reliability of the Imamate lineage. This establishes that the Imam’s martyrdom is not merely a historical event but a theological certainty essential for validating the subsequent Imams.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: The assertion that Amirul Momineen (a.s) is alive is of an obdurate person,
for the knowledge of his death and martyrdom is more famed than the story of the death of anyone else. To doubt his death encourages doubting the death of the Prophet and all of his companions.

Furthermore, his final will and the prediction of the Prophet (s) that you will be killed and that your beard will be dyed with your blood also invalidates this claim. These are facts that do not require us to bring narrations to prove them.
